data.narrative:
Bright Machines, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $300M+ to date, is valued within a comp universe of one public company and eight private peers in the robotics and manufacturing sector. The peer set includes three same-stage companies: Hadrian ($1.6B), Agile Robots ($1.0B), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B), alongside later-stage players Divergent and Exotec.

Two valuation methods triangulate the fair value range. The stage-progression approach applies a 1.7x multiplier to the $300M total raised proxy, implying $510M. The peer-median method yields $1.0B based on three Series C robotics companies, with a range spanning $1.0B to $1.6B. The median of these peer valuations ($1.0B) exceeds the stage-based result by $490M, reflecting sector-specific growth expectations and capital intensity typical of advanced manufacturing.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $434M (low), $755M (median), and $1.1B (high). Key uncertainties include revenue scale and growth trajectory relative to peers—the gap between stage-based and peer-median methods suggests significant dispersion in how the market values robotics companies at this stage. The peer set, though limited to three same-stage comparables, constrains confidence in the upper end of the range. Revenue multiples and path to profitability remain material drivers not directly addressed by this analysis.
